scope: Crypto Lending repository application, wallet-validation, smart-lending external evidence, data-plane, operator, and supply-chain boundaries

classificationLevels.name: PUBLIC
classificationLevels.handling: May be intentionally disclosed, but integrity and provenance controls still apply.

classificationLevels.name: INTERNAL
classificationLevels.handling: Limited to personnel and systems with an operational need; never assume public disclosure is harmless.

classificationLevels.name: CONFIDENTIAL
classificationLevels.handling: Need-to-know access, encrypted transport and storage, bounded retention, and no unrestricted exports.

classificationLevels.name: RESTRICTED
classificationLevels.handling: Customer, authentication, wallet, financial, or security-sensitive data with least-privilege access and explicit lifecycle approval.

classificationLevels.name: PROHIBITED
classificationLevels.handling: Must never enter application persistence, logs, analytics, source control, Jira, or review evidence.

secretInventory.name: OIDC public-client PKCE verifier and authorization transaction secrets
secretInventory.injection: Fresh server-generated 256-bit state, nonce, PKCE verifier, and browser binding for every authorization transaction; the selected Cognito public client has no client credential
secretInventory.storage: Short-lived authenticated-encryption cookie and API memory only; PostgreSQL stores purpose-separated digests rather than the raw values
secretInventory.rotation: Each transaction is single-use and expires; pre-authentication sealing-key overlap and replay-state retention remain separately governed

secretInventory.name: OIDC identity HMAC key
secretInventory.injection: The zero-desired-count production API task selects only the canonical bounded AUTH_IDENTITY_HMAC_KEY_RING_JSON field from an operator-supplied selector-free Secrets Manager ARN at the exact shared immutable VersionId; NODE_ENV is production, LOCAL_DEMO_MODE and legacy identity ID/key fields are forbidden, and the template provisions no secret, key, or running task
secretInventory.storage: Memory only; PostgreSQL stores the current versioned subject digest and append-only provider/issuer/account-bound digest aliases, never subjects or HMAC material
secretInventory.rotation: Migration 0025 installs a dormant accepted-read/active-write policy, concurrent login alias backfill, aggregate retirement gate, and safe rollback refusal; the deployment guard preserves the shared-secret ARN/VersionId/KMS tuple, while a dedicated version-transition guard, external custody, activation, deployed exercise, and predecessor destruction remain blocked

secretInventory.name: Pre-authentication seal, session, and CSRF keys
secretInventory.injection: The zero-desired-count production API task selects AUTH_PREAUTH_SEAL_KEY plus purpose-distinct canonical AUTH_SESSION_HMAC_KEY_RING_JSON and AUTH_CSRF_HMAC_KEY_RING_JSON fields from an operator-supplied selector-free Secrets Manager ARN at the exact shared immutable VersionId; NODE_ENV is production, LOCAL_DEMO_MODE and legacy session/CSRF ID/key fields are forbidden, and the template provisions no secret, key, or running task
secretInventory.storage: Memory only; PostgreSQL stores keyed digests
secretInventory.rotation: Pre-authentication supports one bounded decrypt-only predecessor; migration 0025 locally enforces session/CSRF candidate overlap, matching-version CSRF, successor active writes, replay-before-mutation binding, cross-version rate limits, aggregate retirement gates, and rollback refusal; a dedicated shared-secret VersionId transition guard, external custody, and deployed rotation remain blocked

secretInventory.name: API, worker, and migration database credentials
secretInventory.injection: Workload-specific managed secret references with separate database LOGIN roles
secretInventory.storage: Designed Secrets Manager resources; never source control or logs
secretInventory.rotation: Inactive-slot installation, authentication, task replacement, and old-slot denial

secretInventory.name: Redis ACL credentials
secretInventory.injection: Exact-VersionId API A/B and operator-only managed secret references; worker and migration reject Redis configuration
secretInventory.storage: Designed managed secret plus Redis ACL digest; no plaintext repository value
secretInventory.rotation: A/B slots use the reviewed transition chain; the separately immutable operator version requires a dedicated future transition before rotation

secretInventory.name: AWS workload credentials and KMS key authority
secretInventory.injection: Ephemeral task-role credentials; KMS permissions constrained by service and resource
secretInventory.storage: No static AWS keys in application configuration or CI
secretInventory.rotation: Platform-managed credentials; KMS lifecycle requires explicit retention and deletion approval

secretInventory.name: TLS private keys
secretInventory.injection: Managed certificate service or absolute operator-provided local path
secretInventory.storage: Managed certificate-provider custody, or an ignored operator-restricted local PEM loaded into wallet-server memory; never committed or retained in evidence
secretInventory.rotation: Managed certificate renewal or explicit local test-certificate replacement

secretInventory.name: Wallet-validation access credential
secretInventory.storage: Ignored operator environment and wallet-server memory; only a derived host-only session cookie reaches the browser
secretInventory.rotation: Replace before each authorized execution and close the isolated browser profile

secretInventory.name: RDS bootstrap or master database credential
consumers: Amazon RDS managed control plane and database boundary
Separately authorized database bootstrap operator only
secretInventory.injection: RDS-managed Secrets Manager boundary whose compatibility output contains only the ARN; separate IAM and KMS authorization is required, checked-in application task definitions omit it, and migration-task use is prohibited but still requires deployed origin and IAM-denial evidence
secretInventory.storage: RDS-managed secret encrypted with the application data customer-managed KMS key and the database verifier; lifecycle-coupled to the database and never application configuration, logs, or review evidence
secretInventory.rotation: RDS-owned default seven-day managed rotation through the RDS lifecycle only; authorized results belong to a nested schema-v1 RDS_MASTER_LIFECYCLE_EVIDENCE record covered by the outer two-role-signed schema-v2 bundle. Its primary database, resource, managed-secret, and application-key identities exactly match the schema-v2 target registry's closed rds block and v2 target digest; active statuses, AWSPREVIOUS/AWSCURRENT stages, and ordered access/rotation/restore timestamps are closed fields. Schema-v1 supportingCapture metadata commits to the separately retained canonical sanitized capture through captureSha256; validation does not open that file, so both roles independently calculate and match the digest before signing. Repository/no-bundle or forged/unbranded input emits RDS_MASTER_LIFECYCLE_EVIDENCE_MISSING; malformed, already stale, or counterfeit material is rejected before a report as PRODUCTION_PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE_BUNDLE_INVALID; later staleness restores the RDS blocker and can additionally invalidate a bound public-authority decision

secretInventory.name: Ledger capability and raw idempotency bearer material
secretInventory.injection: Purpose-specific 256-bit capability and caller-supplied idempotency value cross only the fixed ledger command boundary
secretInventory.storage: Raw values are transient process and PostgreSQL parameter material; only purpose-separated capability and idempotency digests persist
secretInventory.rotation: Capability is one-use and expires; issuer custody, revocation, entropy policy, and idempotency lifecycle require independent review

secretInventory.name: Jira API credential
secretInventory.injection: Ignored operator-local Jira environment file or process environment
secretInventory.storage: Atlassian custody and ignored local operator storage; never repository, logs, ticket content, or review artifacts
secretInventory.rotation: Revoke and replace through Atlassian after exposure, operator change, or policy expiry

secretInventory.name: Ephemeral GitHub Actions repository token
consumers: GitHub-hosted workflow checkout and repository read boundary
secretInventory.injection: GitHub-managed per-job token with workflow-level contents read permission
secretInventory.storage: GitHub runner memory only; checkout persistence is disabled and no provider or cloud credential is configured
secretInventory.rotation: GitHub-managed per-job issuance and expiry; repository permissions and workflow changes require review

secretInventory.name: Wallet registration canonical-identity HMAC key
secretInventory.injection: The zero-desired-count production API service is disabled by default; its task selects only WALLET_IDENTITY_HMAC_KEY_RING_JSON from an operator-supplied selector-free Secrets Manager ARN at the exact shared immutable VersionId, requires NODE_ENV=production, omits LOCAL_DEMO_MODE and legacy version/key fields, and provisions no secret or key, while local tests create non-production 32-byte base64url fixtures in process only
secretInventory.storage: Opaque API process-memory wrapper backed by a WeakMap; PostgreSQL stores only the version and purpose-separated keyed canonical-address digest
secretInventory.rotation: Migration 0022 installs a dormant accepted-read/active-write identity policy, complete version-sorted aliases, conflict-safe cutover checks, revocation synchronization, retirement readiness, and rollback refusal; a dedicated shared-secret VersionId transition guard, schema-owner activation, external custody, a deployed drill, old-key retirement, KAN-50, and KAN-235 review remain production gates

secretInventory.name: Wallet ownership-challenge HMAC key
secretInventory.injection: The zero-desired-count production API service is disabled by default; its task selects only WALLET_CHALLENGE_HMAC_KEY_RING_JSON from an operator-supplied selector-free Secrets Manager ARN at the exact shared immutable VersionId, requires NODE_ENV=production, omits LOCAL_DEMO_MODE and legacy version/key fields, and provisions no secret or key, while local tests create non-production 32-byte base64url fixtures in process only
secretInventory.storage: Opaque API process-memory wrapper backed by a WeakMap; PostgreSQL stores only versioned account-binding, domain, message, nonce, and rate-limit digests
secretInventory.rotation: The bounded local ring issues with one active version and reads retained challenge state by its exact accepted version, but a dedicated shared-secret VersionId transition guard, external custody, a staged overlap covering every unexpired challenge and replay tombstone, deployed retirement evidence, KAN-50, and KAN-235 review remain production gates

secretInventory.name: Wallet registration challenge-binding, address, and metadata AES-256-GCM keys
secretInventory.injection: The zero-desired-count production API service is disabled by default; its task selects only WALLET_METADATA_SEAL_KEY_RING_JSON from an operator-supplied selector-free Secrets Manager ARN at the exact shared immutable VersionId, requires NODE_ENV=production, omits LOCAL_DEMO_MODE and legacy version/key fields, and provisions no secret or key, while local tests create non-production 32-byte base64url fixtures in process only
secretInventory.storage: Opaque API process-memory wrapper backed by a WeakMap; PostgreSQL stores versioned ciphertext, random IV, and authentication tag bound to the challenge or wallet row, account, network, address digest, and field through authenticated additional data
secretInventory.rotation: The bounded local ring supports accepted decrypt versions and one active write version; migration 0024 adds a dormant schema-owner-only, audited, atomic rewrap and retirement-readiness boundary with rollback refusal, while a dedicated shared-secret VersionId transition guard, custody, authorized activation, a deployed drill, old-key retirement, KAN-50, and KAN-235 review remain gates

secretInventory.name: Optional LI.FI server API authentication credential
consumers: Smart-lending LI.FI external-feed adapter in an explicitly approved non-production exercise
secretInventory.injection: Optional server-only SMART_LENDING_LIFI_API_KEY environment value from separately authorized managed custody; absent by default and production activation is rejected
secretInventory.storage: LI.FI provider custody and API process memory only when configured; never browser, query string, application persistence, logs, source, or review evidence
secretInventory.rotation: Revoke and replace through LI.FI after exposure, personnel or processor change, or policy expiry; verify old-value denial and replace runtime tasks

secretInventory.name: Production technical-evidence and public-launch decision signing keys
consumers: Separately accountable evidence issuers and launch authorities
secretInventory.injection: Only role-scoped Ed25519 public verification keys may enter the reviewed source registries; production registries remain empty until a separately reviewed key-enrollment change
secretInventory.storage: Private signing keys remain in separately approved external custody and must never enter this repository, CI artifacts, application configuration, logs, or evidence payloads
secretInventory.rotation: Short-lived signed decisions plus key validity, status, one-role scope, revocation, replacement, and re-signing of the exact candidate and target; compromise invalidates every affected decision

threats.scenario: An attacker swaps an OIDC callback, replays state, or links an identity by mutable profile data to take over another account.
mitigations: Authorization Code plus PKCE, nonce, state, and a distinct browser-binding cookie
One-use atomic login attempts and exact case-sensitive issuer plus subject-digest identity mapping
Profile email is never an identity-linking key
threats.residualRisk: Managed-provider behavior, recovery policy, MFA, and independent verification are not proven locally.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 independent verification and managed-provider acceptance

threats.scenario: A stolen, replayed, cross-site, or ambiguously parsed session credential is used to impersonate a customer or force repeated login.
mitigations: Host-only Secure HttpOnly cookies, exact Origin and session-bound CSRF validation
Hashed server-side credentials, dedicated rotation endpoint, predecessor replay detection, and family revocation
Trusted single-proxy source-address policy and fixed-window rate limits
threats.residualRisk: Deployed proxy ranges, edge controls, and distributed abuse behavior require environment evidence.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 deployment and abuse review

threats.scenario: A customer reads or updates another account profile, or private profile fields leak through cache, logs, or error responses.
mitigations: Verified current-principal ownership rather than request-selected account identifiers
Self-only profile service and privacy interceptor
Structured logging field allowlist excludes contact and residency data
threats.residualRisk: Independent authorization, cache, and privacy review has not been performed against a deployed candidate.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 independent BOLA and response-cache review

threats.scenario: Rotating identity or cookie cryptographic material without overlap reinterprets identities, invalidates sessions, or permits duplicate accounts.
mitigations: Canonical purpose-distinct key rings contain at most three sorted numeric versions, select one active write key, reject legacy production keys, and never serialize key material
Migration 0025 atomically maps OIDC digest aliases, binds session and CSRF candidates before lifecycle/replay mutation, charges every rate-limit candidate, and exposes aggregate-only retirement gates
Migration-owned policies remain at version one until a staged schema-owner activation; stale readers fail closed after an active-version flip and rollback refuses after use
threats.residualRisk: The production task pins fail-closed ring selectors to one exact shared-secret VersionId but remains disabled by default and provisions no key; no dedicated current-to-target auth/wallet version-transition guard, external custody, deployed cutover, recovery, or retirement evidence exists, and old single-digest function grants must be removed only after the new fleet is proven.
threats.followUp: Implement and independently review the shared-secret VersionId transition guard, authorize and stage externally custodied ring values, perform the staged non-production rotation drill, prove old-function denial, and obtain KAN-50/KAN-235 custody and independent review

threats.scenario: A malicious wallet or provider spoofs brand, account, chain, network, or session scope and is treated as trusted ownership evidence.
mitigations: Explicit connector choice, chain-qualified accounts, testnet allowlists, and fail-closed scope validation
Supported assets normalize only through exact environment, network ID, and contract or mint identity
Provider metadata is never an authentication signal
threats.residualRisk: Real-wallet behavior and trusted connector chain attestation remain unverified.
threats.followUp: KAN-223 independent wallet review and future connector chain attestation

threats.scenario: A stale, wrong-user, cross-origin, cross-network, or replayed wallet proof attaches an address to the wrong account, or a registration proof is later treated as login or transaction authority.
mitigations: The server issues a short-lived CSPRNG challenge bound to the authenticated account, exact origin and URI, operation, registry network, chain-qualified canonical address, and one-use challenge identifier
EVM ERC-4361 and ERC-191 or Solana SIWS and Ed25519 verification checks the exact message, nonce, address, network, domain, user binding, and expiry before registration

Owner-scoped database functions retain keyed challenge digests and an AES-GCM sealed binding record rather than raw nonce, signed message, or signature; row-locked expiry and other terminal updates destroy the sealed record, audit the outcome, consume success once, record replay or rejection outcomes, and enforce one active account owner for each network-qualified address digest

A verified proof establishes registration ownership only: it neither creates an authentication session nor authorizes a financial transaction, and contract-wallet verification fails closed without a separately approved RPC verifier
threats.residualRisk: The local proof and persistence boundary covers wallet registration only; real-wallet behavior, deployed database concurrency, production key custody, contract-wallet RPC verification, privacy retention, and independent review remain unproven, and no login or transaction authority is granted.
threats.followUp: KAN-223/KAN-235 independent wallet, privacy, key-custody, and deployed-concurrency review; any wallet login, contract-wallet RPC, or transaction authorization needs a distinct approved design

threats.scenario: A seed phrase, private key, pairing URI, raw signature, wallet address, or provider telemetry enters logs, evidence, source control, or a third party.
mitigations: Private keys and seed phrases are prohibited from collection
Raw wallet proof material is memory-only and evidence export is schema-restricted
Repository history scanner and structured logging policy reject secret and wallet-proof material
threats.residualRisk: Vendor telemetry, browser storage, manual exports, and real-wallet network evidence require independent review.
threats.followUp: KAN-223/KAN-235 network, privacy, and evidence review

threats.scenario: An unauthorized caller posts, reverses, mutates, truncates, or directly edits financial records.
mitigations: Purpose-bound one-use capability digests authorize sealed plans
Owner-only append-only tables and fixed SECURITY DEFINER functions
API receives exact EXECUTE grants and worker receives no ledger table access
threats.residualRisk: Database-owner and break-glass access can bypass application controls and has no deployed independent evidence.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 privilege and mutation review

threats.scenario: Retries or concurrent requests create duplicate journals, contradictory lifecycle events, or an outbox message without its financial result.
mitigations: Immutable idempotency identity and result
Journal, lifecycle event, command result, and outbox enqueue commit atomically
Outbox rows use immutable job IDs; any future side-effecting consumer must persist deduplication before enablement
The dormant reviewed-job dispatcher requires the complete three-contract handler registry and rejects malformed, legacy, unknown, or non-launch-network jobs before selecting a handler
threats.residualRisk: Provider-side idempotency, ambiguous outcomes, and reconciliation are outside the current local database boundary.
threats.followUp: Provider submission and reconciliation adapter review

threats.scenario: A spoofed token, wrong chain label, stale price, or nominal one-dollar assumption creates an incorrect financial valuation.
mitigations: Issuer-reviewed stablecoin identity registry rejects wrong network and unconfigured contracts or mints
Ledger requires explicit valuation availability and immutable recognition evidence
New observations cannot select an older registry snapshot

The deterministic KAN-66 evaluator uses bounded integer arithmetic, caps upside at one dollar, preserves downside, rejects stale, conflicting, or malformed evidence, and explicitly classifies depeg state

Migration 0019 records append-only exact-asset depeg latch and clear events, maintains a sticky guarded projection with deterministic revisions and fingerprints, and limits runtime capabilities to read, latch, or separately authorized clear operations
Clear admission requires a classifier-approved recovery, a one-use 15-minute authorization bound to the exact latch revision and evidence fingerprint, and distinct maker and checker identities
threats.residualRisk: Trusted live Pyth and Chainlink observation adapters, approved feed identities and heartbeat evidence, a cryptographic issuer and verifier for Risk clear authorizations, deployed monitoring, and live recovery exercises are absent.
threats.followUp: Complete KAN-252 independent provider and valuation approval, implement the approved live observation boundary and cryptographic clear authority, then exercise stale, conflict, depeg, authorization replay, and recovery behavior before activation

threats.scenario: A chain reorganization, provider outage, ambiguous submission, or delayed observation is represented as final or resubmitted unsafely.
mitigations: No production provider submission or indexing path is enabled yet
A dormant Aave Ethereum checkpoint boundary preserves source-scoped append-only finalized decisions, last-good facts, optimistic revisions, and sticky quarantine
Continuity backfill and quarantine recovery require two distinct agreeing sources across every contiguous block, are bounded to 64 blocks, and cannot roll back or skip history
Single-use recovery authorization is bound to operation, sources, chain, deployment, current state, target, approver, nonce, issuance time, and an exclusive expiry before the locked database mutation
threats.residualRisk: The local recovery contract covers only the dormant Aave Ethereum read checkpoint. Approved independent live readers, source-pair identity, a cryptographic authorization issuer and verifier, live finality and reorg exercises, Solana indexing, and transaction unknown-outcome reconciliation are absent.
threats.followUp: Approve and implement the real read sources, source-pair registry, authorization service, and live recovery drill; separately implement network-specific indexing plus idempotent submission and unknown-outcome reconciliation before enabling chain processing

threats.scenario: An operator, workload, or migration principal gains wildcard cloud, secret, KMS, database, Redis, or financial capability.
mitigations: Workload-specific IAM, secret, network, database, and Redis matrices
Separate migration identity and deny-by-default application database grants
Static mutation validators reject wildcard and cross-scope permissions
threats.residualRisk: Static policies do not prove live IAM, secret, database, or break-glass behavior.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 and separately authorized deployed IAM/secret-rotation validation

threats.scenario: An unreviewed deployment or cleanup exposes a public service, destroys protected state, retains billable resources, or incurs unauthorized spend.
mitigations: Local-first plan/validate boundaries and zero desired count for fresh plans
Separate billing, deployment, retention, and deletion authorities
No cloud mutation in default validation or CI
threats.residualRisk: Commercial approval, operator separation, retention choices, and cleanup must be enforced for any actual deployment.
threats.followUp: Explicit commercial and deployment authorization before any cloud action

threats.scenario: An administrator performs a sensitive action without durable attribution, or incident queries expose customer, credential, wallet, or financial data.
mitigations: Append-only domain audit records and structured correlation identifiers
Event-specific log allowlists and default 14-day operational-log retention
Admin product routes are not implemented or exposed
threats.residualRisk: Administrative RBAC, masking, audit-query access, and deployed log-access evidence are not implemented.
threats.followUp: KAN-235/KAN-249 deployed access, query, and retention verification plus future admin RBAC

threats.scenario: A customer credential, forged staff role, or insufficiently authenticated support user reaches an administrator-only route or action.
mitigations: No administrator module, controller, role, or route is currently wired into the application
A future separate namespace must use server-owned role assignment, deny-by-default authorization, step-up readiness, and immutable allow-and-deny audit
threats.residualRisk: Deny-by-absence prevents current exposure but does not supply the required staff identity, role, step-up, or authorization design.
threats.followUp: FND-008 and OPS-001 administrator authentication and authorization boundary before any route is exposed

threats.scenario: A malicious or compromised staff user enumerates customers, performs unrestricted contact lookup, exports bulk PII or financial data, or bypasses masking and purpose audit.
mitigations: No product administrator search, bulk export, or customer financial query surface exists
Future lookup must use exact identifiers or controlled contact search, bounded pagination and rate limits, field masking, purpose and role checks, and immutable query audit
threats.residualRisk: No implemented staff-query policy, masking contract, privacy approval, or immutable administrator lookup audit exists.
threats.followUp: FND-008, OPS-002, OPS-003, and KAN-44 controlled support and financial query boundaries

threats.scenario: An operator edits or deletes case history, performs an unapproved financial correction, or uses administrator tooling to bypass immutable ledger reversal controls.
mitigations: No product case-management or financial override surface exists
The ledger exposes immutable lifecycle facts and exact reversal boundaries rather than mutable administrator corrections
Future cases require deduplicated identity, assignment and state history, mandatory resolution evidence, separation of duties, and immutable action audit
threats.residualRisk: The case workflow, maker-checker policy, administrator audit, and controlled financial-recovery path are not implemented.
threats.followUp: OPS-004 case lifecycle and reviewed ledger reversal or recovery integration

threats.scenario: A credential, private key, seed phrase, connection string, raw token, or signature enters Git history, application logs, build output, or review evidence.
mitigations: History-aware repository secret scanner and mutation tests
API and worker application-owned structured logging source policy and field allowlists

Next.js Node instrumentation records request and fatal failures through a closed application schema without reading raw paths, headers, error messages, causes, stacks, digests, or provider responses; source-policy tests reject direct application console and stream output
Workload-specific managed secret references; no cloud, provider, or runtime credentials in CI, and the ephemeral GitHub token is read-only and not persisted
The optional LI.FI credential is server-only, absent by default, excluded from query strings, and unreachable in production while external-feed activation is rejected
threats.residualRisk: Framework-owned diagnostics, ignored or untracked local files, runtime memory, external systems, third-party processors, and deployed logs remain outside the complete local application source-policy boundary.
threats.followUp: KAN-235 independent source and final-image review plus an authorized deployed exercise covering framework diagnostics, runtime delivery, access denial, retention, search, and deletion without prohibited values

threats.scenario: Secret rotation reuses a retained slot, leaves old credentials valid, breaks identity mapping, gives one workload another workload's secret, or loses the RDS-managed master-secret binding during database recovery.
mitigations: Fixed workload-to-secret capability matrices and separate database roles
